name: NEWF World Title
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated seven-reign chain from Dirt's founding win at NEWF: The Beginning (21 June 1998) to Most Holy's win over Alex Star on 1 December 1998, each entry dated to both winning and losing sides. Two reigns anchor the ledger here: the founding reign, and Most Holy's win, independently confirmed by the fed's own served Pandemonium PPV recap — the same Iron Man Match the title-history page's own final entry records.

name: NEWF World Tag Team Titles
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated 8-reign chain for this belt, from TKO's founding win at NEWF: The Beginning (21 June 1998) onward. Present holders per the title-history page's own last entry; the fed's own served Pandemonium PPV recap independently confirms them still champions three weeks later, retaining against Conveyors Of Pain.

name: NEWF U.S. Title
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated 15-reign chain for this belt, from Bolo Yeung's founding win at NEWF: The Beginning (21 June 1998) onward. The title-history page's own footnote records the belt vacated the same day, "when Speed Racer dumped it to pursue the World Title." The fed's own served Pandemonium PPV recap, dated the same day, does not itself narrate a vacating — it shows Speed Racer defending and retaining the U.S. Title in a straight match against Sinister Sean Blake that same night (Commissioner Clayton's own on-air announcement calls him "the U.S. Champ" going into it), and its own introduction for the later World Title main event billed Most Holy — not Speed Racer — as "The U.S. Champion," a discrepancy between the two served primary sources the held record does not otherwise resolve.
